summary: A token name and its value in IBM Plex Mono, with a color swatch when the value is a color. For token tables, before and after values, and the values behind a conflict choice.
whenToUse: Showing a token in a table, a review or a change list: the name, the value as written, and the resolved value when it is an alias.
Before and after a change: the previous value with previous (struck through), then the new value.
Inside a ChoiceCard description, so the reader sees the value each choice keeps.
size sm in dense tables and inside sentences; md everywhere else.
Plain-script pages that build rows as HTML strings use tokenValueHtml() from @bridge-ds/react/dom: the same markup and swatch rules, without React.
whenNotToUse: A command or a snippet the reader copies: use CodeBlock.
A status such as Changed or Removed: use Badge next to the value.
Editing a value: use an Input, and show the TokenValue as the current value next to it.

dos.title: Show the alias and what it resolves to
dos.text: The alias says where the value comes from, the resolved value says what the reader will see. Together they answer both questions in one glance.

dos.title: Pair a previous value with the new one
dos.text: The struck-through value reads as removed, the plain one as the new value. Keep them on one line, old first.

donts.title: Repeating the token name in its own row
donts.text: When the row or column already names the token, drop name and show the value only. The same name twice is noise.

donts.title: A previous value on its own
donts.text: A struck-through value without the new one tells the reader what is gone but not what replaces it.

accessibility: Static text, no interaction: screen readers read the name, the value and the resolved value in order.
The swatch is decorative (aria-hidden): the value text always says the color, so the swatch is never the only signal.
A previous value is wrapped in del, so assistive technology that reports deletions reads it as removed, and it is struck through for sighted readers.
The swatch carries a hairline border, so white and near-background colors still read as a square in both themes.
Long names and aliases break anywhere instead of overflowing a narrow cell.
Plain scripts render the same markup with tokenValueHtml() from @bridge-ds/react/dom.
contentGuidelines: Write the name as the token path, dot separated: color.action.primary.bg, not --color-action-primary-bg.
Write the value as the token file has it: an alias in braces ({color.harbor.700}) or a literal (#0B4A8B, 16px).
Hex values in upper case, so before and after values line up character by character.

anatomy.swatch: Color swatch, only for color values
anatomy.name: Token name
